title: The Drowned Coordinates

features.name: depth-marker
features.desc-on-touch: A chip etched with soundings—the numbers that the harbour's floor broadcasts back, layer by layer. Each reading is a word the water learned to spell.

features.name: coordinate-stack
features.desc-on-touch: Stacked navigation markers, each one a depth-reading the lighthouse kept before it learned to dream. The order of the stack is not ascending or descending—it follows the water's own reckoning.

features.name: signal-tower
features.desc-on-touch: The drowned lighthouse's antenna, still transmitting up through metres of water. The signal is very faint—a hum that remembers when the light still worked.

features.name: memory-chip
features.desc-on-touch: Pinned to the board: a second chip holding the moment the lighthouse went under. It was three minutes past midnight. The reading did not change.

features.name: tidal-glyph
features.desc-on-touch: Not quite writing, not quite diagram: the archive's own attempt to render the tide's grammar, the logic by which water decides what sinks and what rises.

inscription: the harbour keeps its depths in a language of pressure, and the board remembers what the lighthouse forgot

file.name: Harbour_Soundings_Lighthouse_Ledger_Fragmented.mp3
file.note: A recording of the keeper's voice reading coordinates, now waterlogged, frequencies shifted—the depth-numbers themselves have become tidal, rising and falling with the water that claimed the station.
